brief:
A displaced Palestinian who left Gaza describes existence outside the territory as devoid of vitality, where even ordinary moments and significant events have become hollow experiences, We Are Not Numbers reported. The resident characterized the departure as marking a watershed: nothing retains its former significance, from daily routines to major celebrations.

The account reflects the psychological toll of displacement on Palestinians forced to leave Gaza, capturing how dislocation extends beyond physical separation to erode the texture of lived experience itself.
dek: Since leaving Gaza, everything has lost its sparkle, from the smallest routine to the grandest occasion.
title: Gaza exile strips life of meaning, displaced resident says
